claims.text: Overall Green Forest fire in Spain from 22 Jul 2026 00:00 UTC to 23 Jul 2026 00:00 UTC. Forest fire can have a low humanitarian impact based on the burned area and the affected population and their vulnerability. About 8,125 hectares burned and roughly 63 people in the affected area.

GDACS event report (eventid 1029643, episode 6): forest fire in Spain covering a 22-25 July 2026 window, citing about 21,999 hectares burned and roughly 3,667 people in the fire-affected area, assessed as low humanitarian impact based on burned area and affected population.

GDACS event report (eventid 1029643, episode 11): forest fire in Spain, citing about 30,440 hectares burned and roughly 4,330 people in the fire-affected area; still assessed as low (Green) humanitarian impact.

GDACS event report (eventid 1029643, episode 16): forest fire in Spain covering a 22-27 July 2026 window, citing about 63,065 hectares burned and roughly 17,959 people in the fire-affected area, with the most recent thermal-anomaly detection on 27 July 2026; still assessed as low (Green) humanitarian impact.

GDACS event report (eventid 1029643, episode 19): Overall Orange alert for a forest fire in Spain, citing 65,422 hectares burned and 20,161 people in the fire-affected area, with the most recent thermal-anomaly detection on 27 July 2026 — up from Green alert / 63,065 hectares / 17,959 people as of episode 16 (27 July).

description: Multiple simultaneous wildfires broke out southwest of Madrid and in neighbouring Ávila province, Spain, on 22 July 2026 amid extreme heat and strong winds, prompting evacuations in towns including Villa del Prado, San Martín de Valdeiglesias, Pelayos de la Presa and Aldea del Fresno. GDACS escalated its alert from Green to Orange as of episode 19 (27 July 2026), with the burned area at about 65,422 hectares and roughly 20,161 people in the fire-affected area. Spain's Interior Ministry declared a national emergency for the fires on 23-24 July 2026 — widely reported as the first such declaration linked to a wildfire — and evacuation figures well above 10,000 people have been widely reported; neither the national-emergency declaration nor the evacuation count has yet been confirmed by an allowlisted authoritative source.

impact.summary: GDACS's event report (eventid 1029643, episode 19) escalated this fire from a Green to an Orange alert for medium humanitarian impact for a forest fire in Spain, citing 65,422 hectares burned and 20,161 people in the fire-affected area, with the most recent thermal-anomaly detection on 27 July 2026 — up from 63,065 hectares/17,959 people affected as of episode 16. No allowlisted authoritative source has yet published a confirmed death toll or official evacuation count for this fire; Spain's widely reported national emergency declaration (23-24 July) and evacuation figures above 10,000 people come from non-allowlisted media and have not been independently confirmed here.

location.region: Southwestern Madrid region and Ávila province (Villa del Prado, San Martín de Valdeiglesias, Pelayos de la Presa, Aldea del Fresno)
